page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-64 is a compute-oriented virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying host platform features an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Processing capacity is assigned via dedicated allocation, providing 16 physical cores configured with simultaneous multithreading to yield 32 active vCPUs.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, resulting in a density of 2.0 GB per virtual core or 4.0 GB per physical core. This 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio targets execution profiles that prioritize thread capacity over expansive memory pools. The configuration includes no local NVMe or solid-state drives, requiring block storage volumes to support the operating system and persistent file storage. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero dedicated GPUs installed. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-64 provides high processor clock frequency and dedicated compute density without paying for unneeded memory overhead. The principal architectural tradeoff is the absence of local disk, which shifts all I/O requirements to remote storage. This instance is best aligned with compute-bound workloads, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data transformations, and distributed web serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-64 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration pairs these dedicated processing resources with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring persistent data needs to be serviced via external block volumes. Accelerator hardware is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned, while networking features one complimentary public IPv4 address. With its dense core count, high clock rate, and moderate memory allocation, this instance fits parallelized compute-bound tasks, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, batch processing, and distributed application serving.
